node.title: Attempt on Spielman-Teng conjecture on the least singular value of Bernoulli matrices
node.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test whether the constant 1 in front of t is forced by the Gaussian comparison and whether the Bernoulli case can beat it. Result: For the Gaussian matrix Edelman's exact law gives P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - e^{-t^2/2 - t} ~ t as t -> 0, so the constant 1 is exactly the Gaussian density at zero of sqrt n s_n; the conjecture says Bernoulli matrices are no worse than Gaussian up to the exponentially small singular mass. A sufficient condition would be a local limit theorem for sqrt n s_n at zero uniform in n, which is a universality statement at the hard edge (the smallest singular value) and is known (Tao-Vu 2010 hard-edge universality) only in the form P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = (1 - e^{-t^2/2-t}) + O(n^{-c}) for t in a fixed range, which gives the conjecture for t >= n^{-c'} but not for t between c^n and n^{-c'}. The gap regime is exactly the small-ball regime where the Rudelson-Vershynin constant C appears. No improvement obtained. Key identity: Gaussian case: P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - exp(-t^2/2 - t), so the conjectured constant is the Gaussian value. Obstruction: Hard-edge universality covers t >= n^{-c}; the conjecture needs the constant 1 down to exponentially small t.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0029-spielman-teng-conjecture-on-the-least-singular-value-of-bernoulli-matr
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

node.title: Open problem: Spielman-Teng conjecture on the least singular value of Bernoulli matrices
node.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For X with i.i.d. symmetric Bernoulli entries, show P(sqrt n s_n(X) <= t) <= t + c^n for some 0 < c < 1, all large n and all small t >= 0. Source: Bordenave and Chafai: Around the circular law, survey with open problems, Section 7, p. 53. Status notes: Bounded recall 2026-09-07: the t = 0 case, P(s_n = 0) = (1/2 + o(1))^n, was proved by Tikhomirov (Ann. Math. 2020); Rudelson-Vershynin (2008) give C t + c^n with an absolute constant C. Whether C can be taken equal to 1 as conjectured was not found resolved.
Posed in Bordenave and Chafai: Around the circular law, survey with open problems
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

node.title: Least Singular Value of Random Matrices (Rudelson-Vershynin picture)
node.body: For an n by n random matrix A with iid mean-zero sub-Gaussian entries, the smallest singular value satisfies P(s_min(A) <= eps n^{-1/2}) <= C eps + c^n: square random matrices are typically invertible with s_min of order n^{-1/2} (Rudelson-Vershynin), resolving the quantitative invertibility problem behind Spielman-Teng smoothed analysis. For tall m by n matrices with m >= (1 + delta) n, s_min is of order sqrt(m) - sqrt(n-ish) with exponential concentration. The proofs decompose the sphere into compressible vectors (close to sparse - handled by nets and tensorization) and incompressible vectors (reduced to distance-to-subspace and small-ball estimates via the Berry-Esseen or Littlewood-Offord theory of anti-concentration).

node.title: Extreme least singular value of random row submatrices under a bounded fourth moment
node.body:
Let $\xi_m$ be centered real entry laws (a single fixed law is allowed) satisfying, uniformly in $m$, $\operatorname{Var}(\xi_m)=1$, $\|f_{\xi_m}\|_\infty \le K$ for a density $f_{\xi_m}$, and $\mathbb{E}|\xi_m|^4 \le B < \infty$. Let $A_m \in \mathbb{R}^{N_m \times m}$ have iid entries with law $\xi_m$ and $N_m/m \to \gamma > 1$. For a surplus $r_m \ge 0$ put $M_{m,r_m}(A_m) = \min_{T \subset [N_m],\,|T| = m + r_m} \sigma_m((A_m)_T)$ and $k_m = r_m + 1$. If $k_m \log m = o(m)$, then $\frac{k_m}{m}\log M_{m,r_m}(A_m) \to -h(\gamma)$ in probability, where $h(\gamma) = \gamma\log\gamma - (\gamma-1)\log(\gamma-1)$. For fixed $r$ this reads $\frac{1}{m}\log M_{m,r} \to -h(\gamma)/(r+1)$. STATUS, recorded as the source states it and deliberately not upgraded: this is a CANDIDATE COMPLETE PROOF and still requires two independent audits before closure. It weakens the subgaussian hypothesis of the published version (arXiv:2608.07410, Yang-Wen-Shmalo) to a uniform fourth moment, but does NOT retain that paper's explicit $Ce^{-c\sqrt{m}}$ deviation rate or its compact-aspect-ratio uniform almost-sure formulation. The complex analogue, and its factor $1/2$, remain OPEN.
entries iid, centered, variance one
uniformly bounded density
uniformly bounded fourth moment
N_m/m -> gamma > 1
k_m log m = o(m)

metadata.proof_text: The lower estimate (negative second moment plus a bounded-density projection bound and a union bound) never used subgaussian tails. Subgaussianity entered the upper proof in exactly three places: the local-density lower bound, where it only controlled third moments of block sums; Nguyen-Vu sup-norm delocalization for hyperplane normals; and an exponential operator-norm tail in the nearly-parallel-pair lemma. The staged selection argument itself needs only three structural facts: a one-slab lower bound of order $t$, a two-slab upper bound $O(t^2)$ away from parallel normals, and an exponentially sparse exceptional-pair graph. Each of the three uses is replaced locally. For the local density, incompressibility alone suffices: for an incompressible unit vector $u$ the coordinates below $1/\sqrt{\delta m}$ carry Euclidean mass at least $\rho/2$, Rosenthal's inequality at $p=3$ bounds the third moments of the greedy blocks, and the Bobkov-Gotze density Berry-Esseen theorem makes the normalized diffuse sum's density uniformly close to the Gaussian density, giving a density floor $c_* > 0$ on a fixed interval; convolving back the large-coordinate part preserves that floor provided the interval is wide enough to survive the convolution. The uniform fourth moment is then used only to supply a uniform third moment and the operator-norm tightness the staged argument needs.

node.title: Smallest Singular Value of a Square Random Matrix (Rudelson-Vershynin)
node.body:
Let A be an n x n random matrix whose entries are independent, identically distributed, centred, of unit variance and sub-Gaussian (sub-Gaussian norm at most K). Then for every epsilon >= 0, P( s_min(A) <= epsilon n^{-1/2} ) <= C epsilon + c^n, where C > 0 and c in (0,1) depend only on K. So the smallest singular value of a square random matrix is of order n^{-1/2} with high probability - the same order as for the Gaussian case, where Edelman computed the exact law of n s_min(G)^2 - and A is invertible with probability 1 - c^n even for Bernoulli (+-1) entries, for which singularity has positive probability; the c^n term is necessary because two equal rows occur with probability at least 2^{-n} c'. Together with Gordon's bound for tall matrices this settles the invertibility question for the basic random-matrix models.
entries i.i.d., mean zero, variance one, sub-Gaussian with norm at most K
A is square, n x n
C and c depend only on K; the c^n term cannot be removed for discrete entries

metadata.proof_text: The argument (Rudelson and Vershynin 2008, building on Rudelson 2008) splits the unit sphere into compressible vectors, those within a small distance of a sparse vector, and incompressible ones, and bounds inf |A x| over each class. Compressible vectors: a union bound over an epsilon-net of the sparse vectors, each of which has |A x| >= c sqrt(n) with probability 1 - exp(-c n) by a standard concentration argument for a fixed direction, gives the c^n term. Incompressible vectors: for such x a constant fraction of the coordinates has size of order n^{-1/2}, and |A x| is controlled through the distance from a single column of A to the span of the other columns, dist(X_j, H_j), by the geometric inequality inf over incompressible x of |A x| >= c n^{-1/2} min over j of dist(X_j, H_j) in a suitable averaged form. The distance dist(X_j, H_j) = |<X_j, nu>| for a unit normal nu of the hyperplane H_j, independent of X_j; the small-ball probability P(|<X_j, nu>| <= epsilon) is bounded by C epsilon + c^n using the Littlewood-Offord theory of the sum sum_k nu_k xi_k: a random normal nu of a random hyperplane is itself incompressible with high probability, and for an incompressible coefficient vector the sum has small-ball probability O(epsilon + c^n) by the inverse Littlewood-Offord theorem (the arithmetic-structure dichotomy: a large small-ball probability forces the coefficients to be close to a generalised arithmetic progression, which an incompressible random normal is not). Assembling the two classes with a union bound gives C epsilon + c^n. This is a sketch of the structure; the constants and the incompressibility of the random normal are the technical core and are in the cited paper.
metadata.source_revision: standard-theorem-2026-09-03; statement and method outline by the author; references: Rudelson and Vershynin, The Littlewood-Offord problem and invertibility of random matrices, Adv. Math. 218 (2008), Theorem 1.1; Vershynin, Introduction to the non-asymptotic analysis of random matrices, Theorem 5.38 and section 5.6

node.title: Schatten p-norms: the l_p norms of the singular values (nuclear, Frobenius and spectral as cases)
node.body: For a complex m by n matrix A, s_1(A) >= s_2(A) >= ... >= 0 are its singular values (padded with zeros to min(m, n) entries). For 1 <= p < infinity the Schatten p-norm is ||A||_{S_p} = (sum_i s_i(A)^p)^(1/p), and ||A||_{S_infinity} = s_1(A), the spectral norm. Zero singular values do not change the value. These norms are unitarily invariant, ||U A V||_{S_p} = ||A||_{S_p} for unitary U and V, and S_1 is the nuclear (trace) norm, S_2 the Frobenius norm and S_infinity the spectral norm.
